verdicts.reasons:
Blocking:
(1) A has the tallest open band of the three: 130 px against d04's 106 at 373, and 240.6 against 216.7 at 160. The cost comes from a bare "Theme" row stacked above today's line. The one thing A does better, a real section title, moves to B with one CSS rule (VT01).
(2) The 22 px mini chip's accent stripe is an underline. It sits 0.5 px (Default) or 1.5 px (every preset) under the word's baseline and is only 4 px wider than the word. "Ember" reads as an orange hyperlink, and the chain mark plus an underline makes "Default" read as a link right beside the real link, Change.
(3) Under 300 px the open band leaves Change alone on its own row, because the inner grid keeps an empty cell for the visually hidden label.

- The folded row is 34 px; every sibling row is 30.2.
- The title drops 1.9 px when the band folds, and the marker sits 1.4 px off the title's center.
- At 160 px a folded Default takes three rows (72.3 px).

answers.q2_fold_all:
Yes: include the band in Open all, Fold all and Alt-click.

Once VT01 makes the band look like a section, a section-looking row that ignored Fold all would be the one exception on the panel. It would also leave a 111 px block above an otherwise all-folded panel. Folding it loses nothing the owner protects, because the folded row keeps the chip and the scope, so the resolved theme stays on screen.

MEASURED on A, B, C and V:
- Fold all folds sec-theme; Open all opens it; Alt-click on Reading folds it.
- With the band folded, every section row fits the 410 px first screen (the brief's pageH 410; capture iV/V-fold-all.png).
- The toolbar's aria-disabled logic already counts the band (READ pi-shell.js syncFoldBar).
answers.q3_hidden_until_answer:
Yes, it is acceptable, and it is needed.

MEASURED with a 250 ms simulated fold reply, on all variants:
- The band is hidden at about 110 and 220 ms and visible from about 325 ms.
- The answer mark lands at 277 to 291 ms (the cap is 300 ms).
- All sections appear in the same frame.
- A later pick moved no chip.

Without the wait, a remembered fold would pull Reading up by 80 px (111 to 31) after first paint, under the pointer.

The cost: d04 painted the band at once, whereas now only the header shows for up to 300 ms. The header's own face already shows the drawn theme during that wait.

cleanup:
Lab processes: every run used Chrome on port 34019 and pi-sim on ports 34010 to 34017.

Harness hazard, found and handled: on this machine, the chrome.exe PID that cdp.mjs launch() returns (and close() kills) hands off to a child browser process. That child survives close() and keeps the debug port. Each of my first six runs left one behind, and the later runs on the same port silently attached to the first orphan. The results still hold, because every run resets viewport and media emulation on its page (INFERRED).

What I stopped: I checked each orphan's command line (--remote-debugging-port=34019 plus a hw-pi-lab-* profile, created at my run times) and stopped exactly those six browser trees: PIDs 146200, 144396, 40484, 143952, 143652 and 133436. I removed their six profiles: hw-pi-lab-QL76iC, qIz1dB, yZkYmL, bN0kXG, 0U7Oj2 and Zby7Vu.

After the fix: my later scripts (edge.mjs, theme8.mjs) record the child PID and kill it after close(). Final check: zero processes with remote-debugging-port=3401x and no listeners on 34010 to 34019.

Left in place: one Chrome profile from each of my last two runs may remain in %TEMP% as hw-pi-lab-*. I cannot tell them apart from other labs' profiles, so I left every hw-pi-lab-* dir alone.

Suggestion: cdp.mjs close() should kill the child browser (or the whole process tree), or the other reviewers' labs will orphan browsers the same way.

Everything else I wrote is inside C:\Users\stephen\AppData\Local\Temp\hw-tf-visual (scripts, captures, JSON, and the proto-V copy). The repository and the prototype dirs are untouched. I did not touch the Stream Deck app, HWiNFO, the installed plugin or port 23654.
